result.comment:
Story-004 proposes eight observable criteria and eight linked tasks: new sessions default to graph only after real-use evidence, explicit legacy remains available, and existing sessions retain their route. Intent and architecture are unchanged. No checks or real runs are claimed; real-run evidence is absent and remains a delivery prerequisite, with no invented run-count threshold.

Current assembled review: all five stories remain active; none is retired. Preserve the factory's link-only parent index for story-001 through story-005 and keep each full draft on its existing sub-issue. Dependencies are exactly 002 -> 001, 003 -> 002, 004 -> 002 and 003, and 005 -> 004; 001 has none. The set is acyclic and has no dangling references. Supplied records retain acceptance reviews for 001–003. This submission adds 004's acceptance draft; 005 remains at its story review and still needs technical and acceptance work. Therefore this is the current assembled review, not a claim that the whole Plan is complete or ready for implementation.

Shared decisions remain: DOT owns flow, the existing envelope and MCP route are reused, investigation is read-only, one gated fixer handles one defect within three files, the investigator has one question round, and failures do not start repair retries. The settled 002 addition files a plain issue only after a fix grows too large; 003 documents that distinction. Adoption and retirement remain separate; /spike, mode identity and note history stay. Default adoption requires real runs; retirement additionally requires legacy work to finish or be explicitly closed. No numeric real-run threshold is settled. The 004 guide-edit exclusion and resulting older opt-in wording remain recorded limitations.

Only criteria and tasks change on story-004. The factory supplies the exact active references and shared-decision binding and owns parent rendering and publication. Owner review of 004 and remaining 005 work are still required before assembled-plan completion. Input acknowledgment will not establish engineering completion, acceptance, publication or readiness.

draft.name: Graph Spike becomes the default

user_story.actor: An engineer running /spike in a repository
user_story.want: graph Spike to run by default once it has demonstrated its use in real completed runs, while retaining an explicit setting to use the old single-agent Spike
user_story.benefit: I get the bounded investigation and small-fix flow without opting in for each repository, and can fall back to the old behavior if needed
notes: The answer path, fix path and guide must be delivered first.
This changes the default for new Spike sessions. Existing sessions keep the route on which they started.

draft.problem: Graph Spike initially requires each repository to opt in, so users otherwise keep getting the old single-agent behavior. Once real completed runs support adoption, graph Spike should become the normal choice while the old route remains available as a temporary fallback.
in_scope: Make graph Spike the default for new /spike sessions when the repository has not explicitly selected a route.
Keep explicit graph and legacy choices working through the existing temporary repository setting; legacy becomes the deliberate rollback choice.
Preserve the route of sessions already started, including when the default or repository setting changes.
Require evidence from real completed graph Spike runs before the default changes; merging preparatory work alone does not authorize the switch.
not_in_scope: Removing the legacy route, its mode instructions or guidance, or the temporary setting; retirement belongs to story-005.
Changing how graph Spike investigates, asks questions, measures fixes, changes code or reports outcomes.
Changing the Spike guide delivered by story-003.
Changing /spike, the Spike mode identity, or the Research, Plan and Bug flows.

general.decision: Reuse story-001's .litefactory/spike.yaml reader, Spike admission boundary and single default constant. Change its absent-setting default from legacy to graph. Retain the graph and fix path from stories 001 and 002.
general.rationale: internal/config/research.go separates an absent file from an explicit route, and internal/turn/research_admission.go resolves that absence through an application default. Spike needs the same small activation change, not another runner.

general.decision: A retained Spike route wins. At first Spike admission, explicit execution: graph or legacy wins over the application default; only a missing setting selects graph. Read repository configuration from the registered clone. Explicit legacy remains available for newly admitted sessions.
general.rationale: internal/store/research_admission.go:AdmitWorkflowPath inserts once and returns the retained route. Replacing a setting must not silently migrate running or waiting work.

general.decision: Before activation, ensure pre-graph Spike work retains legacy admission and existing graph Spike work retains graph admission. Reuse story-001's compatibility handling and store-owned route access. Never infer graph from a missing row on a session with prior Spike work, and never overwrite a conflicting retained route. Refuse unresolved provenance instead.
general.rationale: Migration 0052 backfills Research history only. Its existence does not prove historical Spike sessions are protected. The reused route table is keyed by session, so cross-mode records also need explicit handling at the dependency boundary.

general.decision: Leave spike.dot, node limits, role access, checks, issue creation and reporting unchanged. Keep the existing /spike interface, graph-policy admission and shared preflight/submit/receipt route. Retain legacy tools and guidance until story-005.
general.rationale: This story changes which implementation starts by default. It grants no new agent authority and adds no workflow branches in Go.

general.decision: Keep the legacy default until real completed opt-in graph Spike runs have a retained adoption record linking source issue/session, shipped revision, provider/CLI context, graph outcome, SPIKE.md and final report. Record failures and missing evidence honestly. Use existing release review; do not add runtime run-count thresholds or automatic rollout.
general.rationale: The retained intent makes real use a delivery prerequisite. Offline tests, successful input receipts and preparatory merges cannot establish it; no numeric threshold was settled.

general.decision: Malformed or unsafe configuration, route-store errors, unavailable graph drivers, invalid graph definitions and unresolved resume provenance stop with explicit errors. Never fall back silently from an admitted graph session to legacy. Preserve context cancellation and existing failure reporting.
general.rationale: Research admission already reports these errors. Automatic fallback could repeat effects, bypass bounds or change permissions mid-session.

general.decision: Deliver after stories 002 and 003, with story-001 transitively supplying admission. Leave the Spike guide untouched as settled; the adoption record must clearly state the new default and that explicit legacy affects new sessions only. Retirement and draining remain story-005.
general.rationale: Adoption and deletion are separate decisions. The older guide's opt-in wording is a known documentation limitation, not permission to widen this story.

data_model.definition: .litefactory/spike.yaml holds execution: graph or execution: legacy; absence delegates to the application default.
data_model.constraints: Keep strict decoding and trusted-clone file protections. Empty, unknown, duplicate or malformed values are errors, not absence.

data_model.definition: The first admitted route is associated with the session and reused across owner replies and restarts.
data_model.constraints: No default-driven rewrite, new table or result-payload change is needed. Historical Spike routes must be established before activation; existing mode provenance must not be overwritten.

service_design.responsibility: The story-001 reader owns strict file decoding; the Spike turn boundary applies its one application default and dispatches using the store-returned route.
service_design.access: Read registered repository configuration; retain existing authorized-launch and graph-resume boundaries. No agent-selected route.

service_design.responsibility: Reuse atomic admission and existing pinned graph execution/resume. Any missing historical-route protection is resolved through store-owned compatibility handling before activation.
service_design.access: All SQL remains in internal/store with context-first calls. Keep existing graph instances, pending effects and owner waits; do not rewrite them for rollback.

solution_design.contract: For new Spike admission: missing setting -> graph; explicit graph -> graph; explicit legacy -> legacy; invalid setting -> error. A retained route overrides later defaults and valid setting changes. Persist route before dispatch and use the returned value.
solution_design.rationale: One selection boundary makes the default reversible for new work while preserving continuity.

solution_design.contract: Continue admitted graph work through its existing graph instance and retained provenance; continue admitted legacy work on legacy. Setting execution: legacy does not convert existing graph work. Recovery and pending publications keep their original identities.
solution_design.rationale: Rollback must not become a second execution of already admitted work or an implicit mode transition.

decisions: Retain default adoption and legacy retirement as separate stories.
Keep the existing repository setting as the rollback control until retirement.
Preserve the existing rule that an admitted session keeps its route.
Change only Spike's application default after real-run evidence is available; reuse story-001 admission and story-002 execution without another graph or protocol.
assumptions: Real completed runs means actual graph Spike use with retained outcomes, not only automated or simulated checks. No fixed run count or observation period has been settled.

This story retains the saved exclusion of guide edits. The guide's temporary activation notes must be understood as describing the earlier opt-in delivery; the adoption record must make the changed default clear.

Spike-specific setting/admission, graph and roles are not yet present in this worktree. Their delivery through stories 001 and 002 is a prerequisite; the named existing Research mechanisms are reuse evidence, not claims that Spike already implements them.
No qualifying real-run evidence was supplied for this review. The architecture can be completed now, but delivery of the default change remains gated on that evidence.
The adoption evidence is a release record reviewed through the existing delivery process, not a new runtime counter, timer or automatic activation service.

criteria.text: After activation, a new /spike session with no spike.yaml selects graph; explicit graph selects graph and explicit legacy selects legacy, using configuration from the registered clone.
criteria.proof_method: Future admission tests will exercise all three selections and a conflicting worktree-local setting, then inspect the retained route and dispatched implementation.

criteria.text: An admitted graph or legacy session keeps its route across default changes, valid setting changes, owner replies and restarts. Admission is persisted before dispatch and the store-returned route is used.
criteria.proof_method: Future store and workflow tests will change settings in both directions, resume waiting sessions and restart execution. Event traces and records will show persistence before dispatch, use of an existing winning route and unchanged graph-instance, pending-effect and publication identities without duplicate effects.

criteria.text: Before activation, historical Spike work is protected: known legacy work continues as legacy, known graph work as graph, and missing or conflicting provenance is never silently assigned graph or overwritten.
criteria.proof_method: Future compatibility tests will seed pre-graph history without an admission row, retained graph work, unknown provenance and conflicting cross-mode records. They will inspect the resolved route or explicit refusal and prove existing records remain unchanged.

criteria.text: Empty, unknown, duplicate, malformed or unsafe settings fail explicitly; route-store failure, unavailable graph driver, invalid graph and unresolved resume provenance cannot silently fall back to legacy. Cancellation remains observable.
criteria.proof_method: Future table-driven admission tests will inject each configuration/runtime fault and cancellation, then assert the reported error or cancellation and absence of unintended legacy or graph dispatch.

criteria.text: The default remains legacy until an adoption record links real completed opt-in graph Spike runs to source issues/sessions, shipped revision, provider/CLI context, outcomes, SPIKE.md and final reports, and records their review through the existing release process.
criteria.proof_method: Before activation, a future release review will follow each real-run reference, verify completion and record failures or missing evidence. It will record the adoption decision before the default-changing delivery. Offline checks, input receipts and preparatory merges cannot substitute; no numeric threshold is introduced.

criteria.text: The adoption record states that missing settings now select graph, explicit legacy remains available for new sessions, and existing sessions keep their route. It identifies unchanged opt-in guide wording as describing the earlier delivery.
criteria.proof_method: A future content review will locate these statements and compare the examples with admission behavior; a diff review will confirm the story-003 guide was not edited.

criteria.text: Activation changes only the existing Spike default and necessary admission compatibility: /spike, mode identity, legacy route/settings/tools, graph DOT/permissions/checks/reporting and shared result protocol remain intact; other modes keep their behavior.
criteria.proof_method: A future diff review will check the scope against delivered dependencies, and existing graph, permission, protocol and other-mode tests will be run. A workflow test will demonstrate both the default graph route and explicit legacy fallback without graph-flow changes in Go.

criteria.text: Stories 002 and 003, including transitive story-001 admission, are delivered before activation; unresolved historical-route protection or missing real-run evidence leaves activation undelivered.
criteria.proof_method: A future delivery review will link the delivered dependency revisions, compatibility results and adoption record, then record make check results for the final change. Missing prerequisites will be listed as blockers rather than marked complete.

tasks.description: Verify delivered stories 002/003 and transitive admission; identify historical-route gaps and record activation prerequisites.
Resolve historical Spike provenance through store-owned compatibility handling; retain existing routes and refuse unresolved/conflicting records without migration to graph.

Add ordinary Go tests for selection, trusted-clone config, strict/unsafe input, persistence-before-dispatch, returned-route handling, historical/cross-mode provenance, runtime faults and cancellation.

Exercise graph/legacy continuations, owner waits and restart with changed settings/defaults; verify retained instance/effect identities and no fallback or duplicate publication. Use ordinary Go workflow tests without integration tags.

Assemble authentic completed opt-in run evidence and the adoption record; submit it through existing release review, record its decision and failures, and leave activation pending if evidence is missing. Do not replace evidence with simulated checks.
After the adoption prerequisite is satisfied, change the one Spike default to graph; preserve explicit choices, retained-route dispatch and all settled flow/permission boundaries.

Verify final default and explicit rollback dispatch against delivered dependencies; inspect the diff for unchanged guide, DOT, legacy controls and other modes; run make check and attach actual results to the delivery review.

Complete the adoption/delivery record with new-session rollback instructions, retained-session limits, guide limitation, dependency revisions and final check results; distinguish missing evidence from completion.
